title: AI Rotoscope Animation Generator
summary: Make rotoscope animation with AI: real human motion traced into ink, pencil or flat colour. Describe the shot or restyle your footage in Flick. Free to try.
body_markdown:
### What is rotoscope animation?


Rotoscope animation is made by drawing over live-action footage frame by frame, so the animated characters keep the real proportions, weight and timing of the filmed actors.


### Who invented rotoscoping?


The rotoscope was invented by the animator Max Fleischer, who patented it in 1917; it projected film frames onto a drawing surface one at a time so they could be traced.


### Can AI do rotoscoping?


Yes. Flick can generate the rotoscoped look from a text description, restyle a frame of your own footage while keeping the pose, and animate the result into a clip.


### What is the difference between rotoscoping and motion capture?


Rotoscoping traces the filmed image itself into drawings, while motion capture records an actor's movement as data that drives a 3D character; both borrow real human motion.


### Why does rotoscope animation look uncanny?


Real human timing and proportions under flat drawn colour can feel neither live action nor cartoon, which is why many rotoscoped films lean into it for dreamlike or unsettling scenes.


### Is the rotoscope generator free?


Yes, it is free to start: the free plan gives 100 credits every week with no credit card, and GPT Image 2.6 and MiniMax H3 Fast both run on it. Restyling a video clip needs the Standard plan ($20 a month).
